title: Turning up reasoning effort helps most models, not all
caption: One line per model across the reasoning settings we ran; higher catches more backdoors. Blue models catch more at their highest setting than their lowest, at a 2% budget; red ones catch fewer. 'medium / default' holds each model's default where the provider names no level.
notes: Grouped by the sign of the lowest-to-highest change at 2%. Two changes are small: Sonnet's +2.9 (paired 95% interval +0.9 to +4.9), since it starts near the top, and Mistral's -1.8 (-5.1 to +1.1), whose interval spans zero.
Flash-Lite catches 20 to 29% at any setting, so nobody would deploy it. It's red as a counterexample, not as a contender.
Monitoring Monitorability already shows that more test-time compute helps weak monitors. What's new here is pricing it against a bigger sibling, and the counterexamples.
Effort labels aren't comparable across providers (see P04). Marnick's dose section re-plots the ladder against tokens actually spent, the fairer x-axis if a reviewer asks.
